mappings.note: Why two things reared alike behave differently -- the poet's proposition that inner disposition decides conduct. Rejected LO-25: no line states it as a findable fact.
Which kind of personality the poet presents through the flower -- his idea behind the figure. Rejected CG-HIN3, which I keep for items that name a device rather than explain the poet's meaning.
Which elements of nature the poem calls equal for both -- a list assembled by close reading (one plant, moonlight, rain, wind). Rejected LO-22: collection, not interpretation.
What change the flower's qualities bring to its surroundings -- scent and colour, stated in the poem. Rejected LO-22: the effect is described, not argued.
The poem's main message -- its usefulness stated whole. Rejected LO-22: the item asks for the message itself, not for the poet's view on a point.
Compare the two AND say whose qualities you would adopt and why -- a written case for a preference. Rejected LO-22: the learner argues a choice rather than agreeing with the poet.
Explication of 'dhang unke ek se hote nahin' -- unpacking the poet's stated idea. Rejected CG-HIN3: no device is named; the demand is the sense of the line.
Which aspect of life the flower's living among thorns shows -- reading the poet's figure as a claim about life. Rejected CG-HIN3: the key answers with meaning, not with poetic technique.
What worth the poet allows to lineage. Rejected LO-20: the item asks the poet's position, not the learner's own reasoning on birth and caste.

How the thorn treats butterflies and bee, then 'express your own view' -- the learner's reasoned reaction to harm done to small creatures, a natural-world issue. Rejected LO-25, which covers only the located behaviour without the personal response.
Explication of the couplet's purport. Rejected CG-HIN3: sense of the lines, not their craft.
Why the poet chose the flower-and-thorn example at all -- the figure's usefulness to his argument. Rejected LO-22, used where the item asks what he thinks rather than why he wrote it so.
Purport of the 'chhed kar kaanta' couplet, which the key takes to its symbolic reading of harmful people. Rejected CG-HIN3: the symbol is explained, not identified as a device.
Who wins true respect in the poet's view -- his thesis. Rejected LO-25: an argued claim.
Who gladdens the heart with scent and colour -- located in the printed extract. Rejected LO-22: no idea under discussion.
Who is an eyesore to all, from the extract. Rejected LO-22: the line says it.
What 'sur' means -- the archaic sense 'deity'. Rejected LO-25: lexical, not a search.
With what the flower opens the bud of the heart -- located in the extract. Rejected LO-28: the phrase is quoted, and 'kali' is glossed in its own item.
Who irks and who adorns -- the extract's paired details. Rejected LO-22: the contrast is stated.
Where the two are born together. Rejected LO-22: the shared birth is the premise.
Who nurtures both, from the extract. Rejected LO-22: stated detail.
How the rain falls on both. Rejected LO-28: 'meh' is glossed in its own item.

Asks what flower and thorn are SYMBOLS of, answered as softness and hardness -- naming how the poem works through pratik. Cited at goal level because no outcome among the 16 covers poetic symbol; LO-26 is folk song and tale specifically.
How the moon treats both and by what evidence -- located in the extract. Rejected LO-22: equal treatment is stated, its lesson asked elsewhere.
What pricks our fingers. Rejected LO-22: bare detail.
What the thorn does to clothes. Rejected LO-28: 'var basan' is glossed in its own item.
Who takes the butterflies in its lap. Rejected LO-22: located detail.
How the thorn affects a human being -- two located harms. Rejected LO-21: narrated harm, no personal response asked.
'What kind of clothes does a person wear', answered 'shreshtha va sundar' -- the item is really decoding 'var basan'. Rejected LO-25: the answer comes from the words, not from a narrative point.
Whose fingers the thorn pierces (the passer-by's). Rejected LO-22: located detail.
Meaning of 'var basan' -- both words literary. Rejected LO-25: lexical demand.
Which part of the butterfly the thorn cuts (its wings). Rejected LO-28: no word is being glossed.
How the thorn damages fine clothes -- located detail. Rejected LO-21: no personal reaction invited.
How the thorn behaves towards butterflies -- the extract's own description. Rejected LO-21, which I used for the version of this item that asks for the learner's view.
What a person's greatness depends on -- the poet's thesis. Rejected LO-25: no line states it as a fact.
Meaning of 'kasar' -- vocabulary. Rejected LO-25: lexical.
What the line about lineage makes clear -- the poet's claim that lineage does not help the unworthy. Rejected LO-25: an inference from the line.
WHY the thorn is called an eyesore -- the poet's reasoning from its nature. Rejected LO-25, used for the bare 'who is the eyesore' item.
WHY the flower adorns the gods -- the key reasons from its qualities and what it symbolises. Rejected LO-25, used for the bare 'where' item.

Meaning of 'meh' -- vocabulary. NOTE: this key gives 'baadal' (cloud), which contradicts the earlier item in this same chapter that keys meh = baarish and megh = baadal; one of the two keys is wrong. Rejected LO-25: lexical either way.
What the poet says disposition arises from (inner tendency) -- his proposition. Rejected LO-25: not a located fact.
What the poet sets out to prove. Rejected LO-24: the item asks his thesis, not the poem's use.
What a person's nature depends on -- the key reasons beyond the poem to upbringing and company, so the poet's idea is being taken up and extended. Rejected LO-25: nothing in the extract lists these.

What the poet means to explain through the two figures -- deeds over birth. Rejected LO-24, which I used for the 'main message' and 'why this example' items so the three near-identical prompts do not all land on one code.
